candidates.exact_span: The following Minimum Quantification Levels (MQL's) are to be used for reporting pollutant data for NPDES permit applications and/or compliance reporting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether MQLs govern only application reporting, only compliance reporting, or both ('and/or') affects which monitoring events they apply to (B), how sub-MQL or non-quantified results are classified for missing-evidence handling (C), and whether reported values must be treated as quantified or non-numeric when compared against separate discharge limits (A).

The stated concentration unit governs conversion and alignment with reported measurements and any separately stated discharge limits; a different unit interpretation would change numeric exceedance determinations (A) and whether a result is treated as adequately quantified versus effectively missing (C).

Two different MQL values are listed for Mercury with only a footnote marker and no footnote text in this segment; choosing 0.0005 versus 0.005 µg/l changes whether mercury results are treated as quantified or below reporting level, which monitoring/reporting thresholds apply (B), and how mercury measurements are compared or classified when no ordinary numeric result is available (C).

The segment header locator is 'part_i' while the page heading identifies 'APPENDIX A of PART II'; resolving which permit part/appendix is authoritative affects whether these MQL-based reporting requirements are treated as applicable compliance obligations for the evaluated facilities.
